cards.text: Back in verse 8, the Teacher gave his big line: “Futility of futilities.” Now the book steps back and talks about the Teacher himself, like the little note at the bottom of a cookie recipe from the person who wrote it. And the first thing it says? He was wise.

cards.question: The Teacher was wise, but he kept all that wisdom to himself.

cards.text: And this man put in the WORK. He pondered, searched out and arranged many proverbs, so he didn't just toss his sayings in a junk drawer and hope for the best. Believe me, friend, I KNOW how that turns out.

cards.question: When the Teacher went searching, what was he looking for?

answers.text: Delightful sayings and accurate words of truth
Secret sayings meant only for the wise
Clever riddles to puzzle the kings

cards.text: Next, the book paints two pictures of what wise words are like. One comes from the field, and one comes from the workshop.

cards.question: The words of the wise are like goads. What does that picture say wise words do to people?

answers.text: They prod people to keep moving
They lull people into a deep rest
They keep people from asking questions

cards.question: The anthologies of the masters are like firmly embedded nails. What does that picture say about those collected sayings?

answers.text: They hold firm and stay put
They bend with every new idea

cards.question: Those firmly embedded nails are driven by a single ___.

cards.text: Then the book speaks to “my son” and gives him one more warning. This one's about books and study.

cards.question: The warning to “my son” says the making of many books will soon come to an end.
The warning goes on: much study ___ the body.

cards.text: Friend, I read ONE oven manual cover to cover. By page forty I needed a nap, a glass of water and somebody to tell me I was gonna be OKAY.
Now, when all has been heard, here comes the conclusion of the matter. Twelve chapters of searching, and the bottom line is this: fear God and keep His commandments.

cards.question: Why should a person fear God and keep His commandments?

answers.text: Because this is the whole duty of man
Because it brings long life and riches
Because the kings of Israel require it

cards.text: And the very last line of the whole book gives one more reason. God will bring every deed into judgment.

cards.question: God will bring every deed into judgment, but anything done in secret is left out.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 1 quotes "Futility of futilities.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: "Back in verse 8…", "Now the book steps back…", "And the first thing it says?" and "He was wise." The limit is 3.

rule.text: **The opening card** can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The Teacher shows up for the first time and the card never says who he is. Ecclesiastes 1:1 calls him the son of David, king in Jerusalem.

rule.text: **New people.** The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The card quotes Ecclesiastes 12:8 ("Futility of futilities") but cites only Ecclesiastes 12:9. The citation should run from the first verse the card uses to the last.

rule.text: **Cite exactly what the card uses.** Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't match the action. In 12:9 the book talks about the Teacher in the third person. A note at the bottom of a recipe from the person who wrote it is the writer speaking, not someone talking about the writer.

rule.text: 2. The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: "And this man put in the WORK.", "He pondered…" and "Believe me, friend, I KNOW how that turns out." Story cards after the opening card can have 1 or 2.

rule.text: **Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.**

findings.problem: The fill in the blank asks the baker to guess the last word of the line ("driven by a single ___"). Nothing before it lets the baker reason their way to "Shepherd." Card 5's setup ("one comes from the workshop") even points toward "Builder."

rule.text: **Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.**

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke. It tells no part of the passage and doesn't move the baker forward. Card 11 already covered 12:12.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: A baker could argue that the wrong answer "Because it brings long life and riches" is right. Proverbs 22:4 says the fear of the LORD brings wealth, honor and life.

rule.text: **No near-matches.** A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: No card ever tells or asks that God's judgment covers every hidden thing "whether good or evil" (12:14). That is the closing detail of the passage and the whole book.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
